import org.mapstruct.Mapping;
import org.springframework.data.domain.Page;

@Mapper(uses = PetMapper.class)
public interface OwnerMapper {

    @Mapping(target = "displayName", expression = "java(toDisplayName(owner))")
    @Mapping(target = "initials", expression = "java(toInitials(owner))")

## Summary

I implemented shared-household assignment for `POST /api/owners`. When a create request sets `sharesHousehold: true`, an owner may join an existing same-lastName/same-address household, and all members share one stable `householdId` that is now returned on the owner response.

**Changes:**

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `householdId` string property to the `Owner` response schema (the DTOs are generated from this).

2. **`Owner.java`** — added the `householdId` field (`@Column(name = "household_id")`) with getter/setter.

3. **Schema files** (`db/hsqldb`, `db/h2`, `db/mysql`, `db/postgres`) — added the `household_id` column. Tests run on hsqldb.

4. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — ignored `householdId` on the `OwnerFieldsDto → Owner` mapping (it's a computed field, not input, mirroring `customerCode`); `toOwnerDto` carries it back out automatically by name.

5. **New `AssignOwnerHousehold.java`** — the core logic. When `sharesHousehold` is true, it finds existing housemates (same lastName + address, normalized case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace — identical to `EnsureUniqueOwnerHousehold`), reuses an existing housemate's `householdId` if one exists, otherwise mints a fresh UUID and back-fills it onto every housemate that lacks one, then stamps the new owner. Leaves `householdId` null when the flag isn't set.

6. **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired the new `assignHousehold` step into the pipeline after `build` (so the `Owner` entity exists) and under `govern: [ transaction ]`, matching the existing convention.

The existing `EnsureUniqueOwnerHousehold` 409-rejection behavior for non-opting creates is untouched; the new step only runs the assignment side. The `coreJoinersShareHouseholdId` acceptance test passes: joiners `b` and `c` end up with the same non-blank `householdId`.
